messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER — PROD: inference-api | high 5xx (>3% 5m). Priority: P2. Pager: jess

jess: oncall here. pulling up dashboards now.

rafa: I see queue_depth jump on autoscaler: ~6500 enqueued requests starting ~2123455800

samir: HPA metrics appear empty. `kubectl get hpa -n inference` shows current metrics 0%/70%, replicas stuck at 2

samir: command + output:
```
$ kubectl get hpa -n inference
NAME                REFERENCE                        TARGETS         MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
inference-runtime   Deployment/inference-runtime    <unknown>/70%   2         50        2
```

mike: metrics-server logs (cut):
```
I0315 12:00:01.123456 1 rest_scraper.go:88] failed to scrape node metrics: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded
I0315 12:00:02.223456 1 rest_scraper.go:88] failed to scrape pod metrics: context deadline exceeded
```

elaine: GPU pools report: eu-west-1-a: 100% util (12/12 GPUs), us-east-1-b: 98% util (23/23 GPUs). Warmup queue length metric `warmup.backlog` = 480

jess: So far root causes to consider:
- metrics-server outage -> HPA can't see metrics -> no autoscale
- warmup-driver stall -> new pods not reporting Ready -> even manual scale might not help until warmup clears
- GPU pool saturation forcing requests to queue

rafa: mitigation plan — quick steps:
1) manual scale deployment to 12 replicas to start accepting requests (if pods can become Ready)
2) trigger warmup-driver restart on warmup-leader to flush backlog
3) temporarily route non-critical traffic to fallback runtime (redwood-small-quant)
4) open a cloud pool expansion request for extra GPU capacity

samir: executing step 1 now:
```
$ kubectl scale deployment/inference-runtime --replicas=12 -n inference
deployment.apps/inference-runtime scaled
``` 

samir: step 2: restarting warmup driver pod `warmup-driver-0` in namespace infra
```
$ kubectl rollout restart daemonset/warmup-driver -n infra
```

(incident-bot): NOTE: reroute policy applied: route /v1/generate fallback to model redwood-small-quant for customers in group=free_tier :warning:

elaine: after warmup restart, warmup.backlog dropped from 480 -> 90 within ~60s. New pods are entering Ready state but some are stuck in Init: `pull sidecar` longer than expected

mike: cloud autoscaler request submitted: `poolctl request add --pool gpu-on-demand --count 6 --region us-east-1` — provider confirmed provisioning but ETA ~7m

jess: customer impact: error rate spike affected a subset of customers hitting large-sequence workloads. Support/Tier 2 notified. No data exposure.

rafa: collecting timeline notes for RCA:
- 2123455600: small metric flakiness observed
- 2123455800: queue depth starts to climb
- 2123456000: metrics-server errors escalate
- 2123456100: HPA stops seeing metrics -> no scale
- 2123456300: GPU pools reach 100% util
- 2123456400: Pager triggered
- 2123456500: manual scale + warmup restart
- 2123456820: fallback routing activated
- 2123457100: extra GPU capacity requested

samir: logs attached (copied snippets):
```
warmup-driver[12]: enqueue=489 failed=no_free_slots retry=3
pod/inference-runtime-xyz Init: pulling sidecar image: pull rate limit
scheduler: failed to bind pod: no available nodes with gpu
```

jess: immediate next actions:
- rafa to own timeline + initial RCA doc (I'll create gist)
- samir to follow up on HPA metrics root cause (metrics-server or horizontal-pod-autoscaler client)
- mike to track cloud pool provisioning and confirm healthy nodes
- elaine to run postmortem eval on warmup-driver throttling

rafa: ack. starting RCA doc: https://r.redwood/rca/2123456789 (placeholder) — I'll include logs, graphs, and owners. tagging @samir @mike @elaine

mike: update: cloud provider reports GPUs provisioned in ~6m, nodes joined cluster at 2123460200, kubelet registered them and pods started scheduling

samir: confirming HPA metrics: metrics-server restarted at 2123459000 via restart job; HPA now reports aggregated CPU 42%/70% and started scaling to target

elaine: warmup backpressure removed, queue depth returned to normal ~120 after routing + added capacity

jess: Customer impact post-incident: P2 resolved, customers affected: ~0.8% of requests in the window, follow-up emails to experimental customers. Will schedule blameless RCA tomorrow 1500 PST.

rafa: recording hypotheses for follow-up tests:
- reproduce metrics-server RPC timeouts under high node count + control-plane load
- test warmup-driver enqueue backpressure handling (configurable max_inflight)
- test HPA fallback when metrics are missing (fallback to external queue length metric)

jess: thanks all. I'll update the incident ticket with the timeline and actions. :white_check_mark:

(incident-bot): INCIDENT RESOLVED — mitigation in place, monitoring for 1h. Logs archived to s3://redwood-incidents/2123456789
